# Code of conduct

## Our standard

Participants are expected to be respectful, precise, and constructive.
Disagreement about evidence, statistics, architecture, or scope is welcome;
harassment and personal attacks are not. This project's whole subject is
reporting its own results honestly, including the retractions, and the same
standard applies to how people treat each other here.

Acceptable behaviour includes:

- critiquing code and claims rather than people;
- stating uncertainty and limitations honestly;
- giving reproducible technical feedback;
- respecting privacy and disclosure boundaries;
- helping newcomers understand the project's constraints.

Unacceptable behaviour includes:

- harassment, threats, discriminatory language, or unwanted sexual attention;
- publishing another person's private information;
- deliberately introducing secrets, personal data, or unsafe instructions;
- sustained disruption, bad-faith review, or retaliation;
- conduct that would reasonably make participation unsafe.

## Scope

This policy applies in repository issues, pull requests, discussions,
reviews, and other spaces where someone represents the project.

## Enforcement

Maintainers may edit or remove contributions, comments, issues, or other
material that violates this policy and may temporarily or permanently
restrict participation.

Report conduct concerns privately through the contact method on the
repository owner's GitHub profile. Do not post sensitive conduct reports
publicly. Platform abuse can also be reported through GitHub's own tools.

Enforcement decisions consider context, severity, impact, prior behaviour,
and the safety of affected participants. Retaliation against a good-faith
reporter is itself a violation.
